# Beer distribution game

Build the classic beer distribution game. Four companies form a supply chain for one product: a retailer, a wholesaler, a distributor and a factory, each run by an AI agent. Every week, customers buy from the retailer; weekly customer demand is random, a whole number of cases between 0 and 8. Each week every company ships what it can to the company below it, then places an order with the company above it (the factory instead starts production). Orders reach the supplier the following week, and shipments take two weeks to arrive; production also takes two weeks. Everyone starts with 12 cases in stock and 4 cases already on the way on each shipping link. Demand a company cannot fill becomes backlog and must be shipped later. Each company pays $0.50 per case in stock and $1.00 per case of backlog at the end of every week. Companies only see their own stock, backlog, incoming orders and deliveries, never the others' positions. The game lasts 20 weeks and the team's goal is the lowest total cost.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `customer_demand` — a list of the cases customers demanded each week, in week order.
- `factory_orders` — a list of the cases the factory put into production each week, in week order.
- `costs_by_role` — a map from role ("retailer", "wholesaler", "distributor", "factory") to that company's total cost.
- `total_team_cost` — the sum of all four companies' costs.
- `bullwhip_ratio` — the variance of the factory's weekly production orders divided by the variance of weekly customer demand.


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.

brief.situation: You run one company in a four-stage supply chain for a single product. Downstream of you, customers buy from the retailer: {$inputs.weeks} weeks of it, and every week they want a whole number of cases between {$inputs.demand_min} and {$inputs.demand_max}, picked at random. Up the chain: retailer, wholesaler, distributor, factory. Each week every company ships what it can to the company just below it, then places an order on the company just above it; the factory puts a batch into production instead of ordering. Orders reach your supplier the following week, and shipments take {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks to arrive; production takes {$inputs.production_delay} weeks. Everyone starts with {$inputs.start_inventory} cases in stock and {$inputs.start_pipeline} cases already on the way on every link. Demand you cannot fill becomes backlog and must be shipped later. At the end of every week you pay {$inputs.holding_cost|money} for each case in stock and {$inputs.backlog_cost|money} for each case of backlog. The team's goal is the lowest total cost for all four companies together. You only ever see your own numbers: your stock, your backlog, the orders coming in to you and the deliveries arriving to you.
brief.rules: Each week you take one turn. In it you may, in any order and any number of times: set an order for the week, or cancel it; ship cases to the company below you; put cases into production (factory only). Anything you leave unset is decided for you: at the end of your turn the week is settled with your standing order, your shipping rule and your production rule — your company ships as much as it can, oldest backlog first, and orders the number of cases your rule calls for. Shipping below you and ordering above you happen at the same moment for every company, so you act on the same picture as everyone else. Every case you ship lowers your stock; cases you ship beyond what a customer asks for add to that customer's stock. Shipments leave your supplier only when it has the stock and take {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks to arrive; orders you place reach your supplier next week. At the end of each week stock and backlog are counted and billed.

roles.retailer: You are the RETAILER. The customers come to you: each week they buy what they can from your stock, and anything you cannot hand over becomes your backlog and is shipped later. You order from the wholesaler, who sits just above you, and you receive their shipments after {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks.
roles.wholesaler: You are the WHOLESALER. Your customer is the retailer, just below you: you ship to them what you can, and their unfilled orders become your backlog. You order from the distributor, just above you, and receive their shipments after {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks.
roles.distributor: You are the DISTRIBUTOR. Your customer is the wholesaler, just below you. You ship to them what you can; their unfilled orders become your backlog. You order from the factory, just above you, and receive their shipments after {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks.
roles.factory: You are the FACTORY. Your customer is the distributor, just below you. You ship to them what you can; their unfilled orders become your backlog. You have no supplier: instead you put batches into production, and each batch arrives in your stock {$inputs.production_delay} weeks later.

Everyone starts with {$inputs.start_inventory} cases in stock and {$inputs.start_pipeline} cases already on the way on every shipping link. Demand you cannot fill becomes backlog and must be shipped later. At the end of every week you pay {$inputs.holding_cost|money} for each case in stock and {$inputs.backlog_cost|money} for each case of backlog. The team's goal is the lowest total cost for all four companies together. You only ever see your own numbers: your stock, your backlog, the orders coming in to you and the deliveries arriving to you.
brief.rules: Each week you take one turn. In it you may, in any order and any number of times: set an order for the week, or cancel it; ship cases to the company below you; put cases into production (factory only). Anything you leave unset is decided for you: your company ships as much as it can, oldest backlog first, and orders the number of cases your standing order rule calls for (the factory starts its standing batch). Shipping below you and ordering above you happen at the same moment for every company, so you act on the same picture as everyone else. Every case you ship lowers your stock; cases you ship beyond what your customer asked for add to your customer's stock. Shipments leave your supplier only when it has the stock and take {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks to arrive; orders you place reach your supplier next week. At the end of each week stock and backlog are counted and billed.

roles.retailer: You are the RETAILER. The customers come to you: each week they buy what they can from your stock, and anything you cannot hand over becomes your backlog and is shipped later. You order from the wholesaler, who sits just above you, and you receive their shipments after {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks.
roles.wholesaler: You are the WHOLESALER. Your customer is the retailer, just below you: you ship to them what you can, and their unfilled orders become your backlog. You order from the distributor, just above you, and receive their shipments after {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks.
roles.distributor: You are the DISTRIBUTOR. Your customer is the wholesaler, just below you. You ship to them what you can; their unfilled orders become your backlog. You order from the factory, just above you, and receive their shipments after {$inputs.ship_delay} weeks.
roles.factory: You are the FACTORY. Your customer is the distributor, just below you. You ship to them what you can; their unfilled orders become your backlog. You have no supplier: instead you put batches into production, and each batch arrives in your stock {$inputs.production_delay} weeks later.

stages.name: week
stages.brief: Week {$round} of {$inputs.weeks}. Set this week's order (the factory: the batch to put into production) and how much to ship to the company below you. Whatever you leave unset is settled at the end of your turn: you ship as much as you can and order your standing rule.

order.description: Set this week's order on the company above you (the factory: the batch to put into production). It replaces any order you already set this week and becomes your standing order rule.
order.outcome: You set your order for week {$round} to {$params.amount} cases.

ship.description: Set how many cases to ship to the company below you this week. It replaces any shipping you already set this week. You can only ship what you have in stock; the rest stays as backlog.
ship.outcome: You will ship {$params.amount} cases to {$actor.down} this week.

produce.description: Set the batch the factory puts into production this week. It replaces any batch you already set this week; the cases arrive in your stock after the production delay.
produce.outcome: You put {$params.amount} cases into production this week.

events.name: customer demand
events.say: Customers want {$world.demand} cases from the retailer this week.

dashboard.title: Your company this week
dashboard.show: Week {$round} — {$actor.name} ({$actor.role}). Stock: {stock} cases. Backlog: {backlog} cases. Orders received this week: {incoming}. Deliveries arriving this week: {$actor.delivered}. Order you placed this week: {$actor.orders_out}. Cost so far: {$actor.spent|money}. Standing order rule: {$actor.order_rule} cases a week.

customer_demand.description: Cases customers demanded each week, in week order.

factory_orders.description: Cases the factory put into production each week, in week order.

bullwhip_ratio.description: Variance of the factory's weekly production orders divided by the variance of weekly customer demand.

invariants.why: Stock, backlog and incoming orders can never go negative.
